key_insight: This study establishes the first U.S. CADASIL natural history cohort, creating a well-characterized monogenic small-vessel disease model to benchmark vascular cognitive impairment and dementia biomarkers, symptoms, and functional outcomes.
clinical_relevance: The baseline data can help standardize future clinical trials and improve understanding of how genotype-linked CADASIL burden relates to cognition, disability, and imaging measures.
method: Cross-sectional baseline analysis from 12 U.S. sites (Oct 2022–Jan 2025).
Adults from families with documented NOTCH3 variants underwent standardized clinical, cognitive, functional, MRI, genetic, and proteomic assessment.
Pathogenic/likely pathogenic NOTCH3 variants were centrally classified into low-, medium-, or high-risk tiers.
evidence_signal: Among 560 baseline participants, the analytic cohort included 343 CADASIL carriers and 116 non-carrier family controls, with group comparisons and multivariable adjustment used to assess differences.
watch_item: Because the cohort is predominantly White and highly educated, generalizability to more diverse populations may be limited.
paper_title: The United States CADASIL Consortium: Baseline Findings from a Natural History Study
